2609.35031.title: PEAR: Progressive Evidence-Based AutoResearch for Industrial Search Systems
2609.35031.paper_summary: AutoResearch improves systems through iterative experimentation: agents propose candidate modifications, evaluate them, and use the results to guide subsequent exploration. Applying this paradigm to industrial search presents two challenges. (1) Common AutoResearch approaches follow a keep-if-better rule, retaining the highest-scoring candidate for subsequent experiments. Under non-stationary traffic, transient gains may be mistaken for persistent improvements, impairing reliable accumulation of search knowledge. (2) Candidate modifications can be evaluated at multiple fidelity levels, from low-cost proxies to online validation, differing in cost, objective alignment, and statistical reliability. Existing methods rely on individual signals or task-specific procedures, lacking a unified basis for using evidence across levels to guide search. We introduce Progressive Evidence-Based AutoResearch (PEAR) with two complementary components. Evidence-driven AutoResearch maintains an independent, hypothesis-guided research state for each strategy task within a predefined objective and intervention scope. Each state evolves through a Plan-Execute-Evaluate-Update transition that links experimentation to context-aware evidence interpretation and hypothesis revision. Confidence-Gated Verifier Ladder organizes evaluation into four levels of increasing fidelity: Offline Replay, Shadow-Traffic Evaluation, Rapid Online Evaluation, and Decision-Grade Online Evaluation. A unified confidence-based gate promotes candidates only when evidence supports a statistically significant positive effect, enabling broad low-cost exploration while reserving costly online experiments for promoted candidates. In a real-world industrial search system, strategies optimized with PEAR significantly increased Main Order/DAU by 2.7336% and 3.2957% relative to their respective baselines in two A/B experiments.
2609.35031.paper_summary_zh: AutoResearch 透過迭代實驗來改進系統：代理提出候選修改，評估它們，並利用結果來指導後續的探索。將這一範式應用於工業搜索面臨兩個挑戰。 (1) 常見的 AutoResearch 方法遵循「若更好則保留」的規則，保留得分最高的候選者以進行後續實驗。在非穩定的流量下，暫時的增益可能會被誤認為持久的改進，從而影響搜索知識的可靠積累。 (2) 候選修改可以在多個精確度層級進行評估，從低成本的代理到在線驗證，這些層級在成本、目標對齊和統計可靠性上有所不同。現有的方法依賴於單一信號或特定任務的程序，缺乏統一的基礎來使用不同層級的證據來指導搜索。我們引入了漸進證據基礎的 AutoResearch（PEAR），其包含兩個互補的組件。證據驅動的 AutoResearch 為每個策略任務維持一個獨立的、假設引導的研究狀態，並在預定的目標和干預範圍內進行。每個狀態通過計劃-執行-評估-更新的轉換進化，將實驗與上下文感知的證據解釋和假設修訂聯繫起來。信心閘驗證者階梯將評估組織為四個逐步提高的精確度層級：離線重播、影子流量評估、快速在線評估和決策級在線評估。統一的基於信心的閘門僅在證據支持統計上顯著的正面效果時推廣候選者，從而實現廣泛的低成本探索，同時將昂貴的在線實驗保留給被推廣的候選者。在一個現實世界的工業搜索系統中，使用 PEAR 優化的策略在兩次 A/B 實驗中相對於各自的基線顯著提高了主訂單/DAU 分別為 2.7336% 和 3.2957%。
